question: How do I get a fee certificate (fee structure / fee breakup certificate) from my college?
answer: Go to the college office (admin/accounts section) and submit a written request letter addressed to the Principal stating the purpose (education loan, scholarship, or income-tax proof). Attach a copy of your college ID card and your fee payment receipts, or a printout of your fee details from the student portal/ERP. The office issues the fee certificate or fee breakup statement, usually by the next working day. It lists the tuition and other fees for the year, which banks and scholarship portals accept as the official cost of study.
documents_required: Written request letter to the Principal stating the purpose
Copy of college ID card
Fee payment receipts OR fee details printout from the student portal/ERP
notes: Kristu Jayanti lists this as 'Bonafide / Student Bank Loan / Fee Breakup & Fee Letter for Income Tax Purpose' needing only a request letter and college ID card; MSSW asks for a written request plus a fee printout from the student login.

form_fields: Purpose of the fee certificate (education loan / scholarship / income tax / other)
Academic year for which the fee breakup is needed
documents_to_upload: Fee payment receipts OR fee details printout from the student portal/ERP
application.after_submission: The accounts/admin office verifies the fee records and issues the fee certificate (fee breakup statement), usually by the next working day. The student collects it from the office or downloads it from the portal if the college issues it online.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by Kristu Jayanti (request letter + ID card) and MSSW (written request + fee printout, issued next working day).

question: I lost my fee receipt. How do I get a duplicate fee receipt?
answer: If you paid online, first check your bank app, UPI app, or payment gateway for the transaction — the UTR/transaction ID and the payment confirmation work as proof, and most portals let you download the receipt again. If you paid by challan at a bank or post office, go back to that branch with the payment date and amount; they can issue a duplicate receipt or a statement. You can also ask the college accounts office to reissue the receipt from its records — carry your college ID card and, if you have them, the payment date, amount, and transaction reference.
documents_required: College ID card
Payment date, amount, and transaction ID/UTR (if paid online)
Challan copy or bank statement showing the payment (if available)
notes: Standard practice confirmed by student Q&A answers: keep the challan/UTR safe, and the place where you paid can reissue the receipt.

question: What is a fee structure, and where do I get it?
answer: A fee structure is the official year-wise or semester-wise breakup of all fees (tuition, exam, library, lab, hostel, and other charges) issued by the college or university. Banks ask for it for education loans, and scholarship portals ask for it to calculate the scholarship amount. Get it from the college accounts office, or from the college website/prospectus — many colleges publish it online. If it is not published, submit a request letter with your college ID card at the accounts office.
documents_required: Request letter (only if the fee structure is not published online)
Copy of college ID card

question: How do I pay my semester or annual college fee?
answer: Most colleges take fees online through the student portal/ERP, SBI Collect, BillDesk, UPI, or net banking. Some also accept a challan paid at a bank. Steps: 1) Log in to the college fee portal. 2) Select the semester/year and fee type. 3) Pay online and save the receipt and transaction ID. 4) Submit a copy of the receipt at the college office if the college asks for it. Pay before the last date — a late fee is charged after the deadline, and the amount varies by college.
documents_required: College ID card or registration number
Online payment receipt (keep a copy)
notes: Exact portal and late-fee amount vary by college; VSSUT's admission notice shows the typical pattern (online registration, BillDesk payment link, printed payment receipt to be submitted).

question: I paid the fee online but there is no receipt or the payment status is unclear. What do I do?
answer: First check the payment status on the portal using your transaction ID/UTR, and check your bank account or UPI app to see if the money was debited. If the money was debited but the portal shows the payment as failed or pending, do NOT pay again immediately — take a screenshot of the debit and the UTR to the college accounts office; they will verify it with the bank and update your record. If the money was not debited, you can safely pay again. Keep the UTR number safe — it is the proof that resolves any dispute later.
documents_required: Transaction ID/UTR
Screenshot of the bank debit
College ID card

question: What is a bonafide certificate and what is it used for?
answer: A bonafide certificate is an official letter from your college or university confirming that you are a genuine, currently enrolled student there — it states your name, course, and period of study. Students use it for: scholarship applications, education loans, visa applications, internships, opening a bank account, bus/train travel concession, and hostel or fee-waiver applications. It is usually valid for 6 months to 1 year from the date of issue, so get a fresh copy when you need it.

question: How do I apply for a bonafide certificate in college? What documents are needed?
answer: Steps: 1) Get the bonafide application form from the college office/admin department, or write a request letter to the Principal stating the purpose. 2) Get it signed by your class teacher/HOD if your college asks for it. 3) Pay the bonafide fee at the accounts office (usually Rs. 20 to Rs. 200, varies by college). 4) Submit the form with the documents below at the admin office. 5) Collect the certificate — most colleges issue it in 1 to 7 working days. Some colleges also take bonafide requests through the student portal/ERP.
documents_required: Bonafide application form OR written request letter to the Principal stating the purpose
Copy of college ID card
Fee receipt of the current academic year
Previous semester mark sheets (sometimes asked)
Passport-size photograph (sometimes asked)
notes: Fee and time vary by college: MSSW issues it the next working day; ICCS collects it after 1 day; other guides report 1-7 days.

form_fields: Purpose of the bonafide certificate (scholarship / loan / visa / internship / concession / other)
documents_to_upload: Fee receipt of the current academic year
Previous semester mark sheets (if the college asks)
application.after_submission: The form goes to the admin office (with HOD/class-teacher signature where required). After the fee is paid, the office prepares the certificate, gets the Principal's signature, and the student collects it — typically in 1 to 7 working days.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by MSSW, ICCS, and Kristu Jayanti office guidelines. Fee (Rs. 20-200) and time vary by college.

question: What is a bonafide certificate with fee details, and how do I get one?
answer: This is a bonafide certificate that also lists the fees you paid — students need it for income-tax proof (for parents claiming education expenses) and for some loan and scholarship verifications. Apply the same way as a normal bonafide certificate, but attach a printout of your fee details taken from the student portal/ERP login along with the written request to the Principal. The college office issues it, usually by the next working day.
documents_required: Written request letter to the Principal
Fee details printout from the student portal/ERP login
Copy of college ID card

documents_to_upload: Fee details printout from the student portal/ERP login
application.after_submission: Issued by the college office, usually by the next working day, with the fee details included on the certificate.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by MSSW guidelines.

question: What is the difference between a bonafide certificate and a study certificate?
answer: A bonafide certificate proves you are CURRENTLY enrolled in the college — it is used for scholarships, loans, visas, and concessions. A study certificate proves you STUDIED at an institution during a stated period (for example, Class 1 to 10, or a specific course) — it is mainly used during counselling and admissions to prove local/non-local status or years of study. For example, KCET counselling asks for a study certificate signed by the concerned Block Education Officer or Deputy Director of Public Instruction. If an office asks for a study certificate, a bonafide certificate will not do — apply for the exact one named.

question: How do I get an income certificate in Andhra Pradesh (MeeSeva)? What documents are needed?
answer: The income certificate is issued by the Revenue Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh, through MeeSeva. Steps: 1) Visit the nearest MeeSeva centre or the MeeSeva portal (ap.meeseva.gov.in) and fill the application form. 2) Submit the documents below. 3) Pay about Rs. 35 at the MeeSeva centre. 4) The application is verified by the VRO/MRI and approved by the MRO. It usually takes 7 to 21 days, and you can download the certificate once approved. The certificate is valid for one year.
documents_required: Duly filled application form with Rs. 2 court fee stamp
Certificate from two different gazetted officers
Duly signed education records
Rs. 10 non-judicial stamp paper declaration (as per G.O. 1551) and Income Tax return if any, or payslip
Residential proof (voter ID, ration card, or electricity bill)
Aadhaar card
Ration card (if available)
Salary certificate from employer (if salaried) OR Pahani land records (if farmer)
Passport-size photograph
notes: All four sources agree on the core list. MeeSeva charges about Rs. 35; the application fee is listed as Rs. 10 in one source.

documents_to_upload: Income proof (salary certificate / payslip / IT return / Pahani land records for farmers)
Certificates from two different gazetted officers
application.after_submission: Apply at a MeeSeva centre or the MeeSeva portal and pay about Rs. 35. The VRO/MRI verifies the details and the MRO approves it. It takes 7 to 21 days; the approved certificate can be downloaded. Valid for one year.
application.notes: Document list confirmed by IndiaFilings, WikiProcedure, CitizenNest, and eSarkari. The two-gazetted-officers requirement is AP-specific.

question: Why do I need an income certificate, and how long is it valid?
answer: An income certificate is the government's official proof of your family's total annual income from all sources. You need it for: AP post-matric scholarships and fee reimbursement, central scholarships on NSP, EWS quota benefits, hostel fee waivers, and education loans. In Andhra Pradesh it is valid for one year, so you must renew it every year — scholarship portals usually ask for a certificate issued in the current financial year. Keep the income figure below the scheme limit (for example, below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year for AP post-matric scholarships).

question: How do I get a Transfer Certificate (TC) from my college?
answer: A TC is issued only when you have completed your course or when the Principal has approved your discontinuation — it is NOT issued to a currently enrolled student. Steps: 1) Get the TC application form from the admin office. 2) Get a no-dues clearance from the department, library, accounts, and hostel (if applicable). 3) Get signatures from the concerned departments and HOD. 4) Pay the TC fee at the accounts office. 5) Submit the form with the documents below. 6) Collect the TC — most colleges issue it in 1 to 5 working days. You must surrender your college ID card when you collect it.
documents_required: TC application form OR request letter signed by the student (and parent/guardian at some colleges)
Copy of marks card / last mark sheet
No-dues certificate from library, lab, accounts, department, and hostel
College ID card (to be surrendered)
Prescribed TC fee payment receipt

form_fields: Course, branch, and year of completion
Reason for leaving (course completed / discontinuation / transfer)
Name of the institution being joined (if any)
documents_to_upload: Copy of marks card / last mark sheet
No-dues certificate from library, lab, accounts, department, and hostel
application.after_submission: The office checks the no-dues clearances and fee payment, prepares the TC, and the student collects it in 1 to 5 working days after surrendering the ID card. A TC is only issued after course completion or approved discontinuation.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by MSSW, ICCS, and Kristu Jayanti office guidelines.

question: How do I get a migration certificate from my university?
answer: A migration certificate is issued by the UNIVERSITY (not your college) and certifies that the university has no objection to you joining another university. You need it when you join PG or further studies in a different university, apply to a foreign university, or for some government jobs. You do NOT need it if you continue in the same university. Steps: 1) Apply at your college exam section or directly at the university Controller of Examinations (CoE) office. 2) Fill the migration application form. 3) Attach the documents below and pay the fee (typically Rs. 100 to Rs. 1,000 depending on the university). 4) It usually takes 15 to 45 working days; some states have a 30-day Right to Service deadline.
documents_required: Migration certificate application form (filled and signed)
Last semester / final year admit card
All semester mark sheets (photocopies; originals for verification)
Provisional certificate or degree certificate (if issued)
Photo ID proof (Aadhaar / PAN / passport)
2 passport-size photographs (some universities ask for 4)
Fee payment receipt
Admission letter of the new institution (if available)
notes: IIPE's official fee table lists migration certificate at Rs. 250 in India; other universities charge Rs. 100 to Rs. 1,000.

form_fields: Reason for migration / name of the new institution
documents_to_upload: Last semester / final year admit card
Provisional certificate or degree certificate (if issued)
application.after_submission: The university (Controller of Examinations / Registrar) verifies academic standing and issues the migration certificate in 15 to 45 working days. It is collected from the university office or sent by post.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by Karvado and RightToInformation guides; IIPE's official fee table lists Rs. 250 for a migration certificate.

question: How do I apply for transcripts from Andhra University?
answer: Andhra University processes transcript requests through its online portal for transcripts, certificates, and genuineness verification (via the Controller of Examinations / Registrar office, Visakhapatnam). Steps: 1) Open the AU online services portal and choose Transcript/Certificate. 2) Fill in your name, university roll/enrolment number, course, year of passing, and number of sets. 3) Upload scanned copies of the documents below. 4) Pay the fee online (the fee depends on how long ago you completed the degree — a higher access fee applies beyond five years). 5) Submit and keep the acknowledgement/reference number for tracking. Typical turnaround reported is about 15 working days. Transcripts are issued in a sealed envelope with the university seal, and can be sent directly to WES/IQAS if you give the reference number.
documents_required: Transcript request form (on the portal)
All semester mark sheets
Degree certificate or provisional certificate
Government-issued ID proof (Aadhaar / passport)
Fee payment receipt
WES / IQAS reference number (if applying for credential evaluation)
Authorisation letter (if someone else collects it for you)
notes: Document list is consistent across three transcript services. The exact AU fee is not published on a page we could retrieve — it is calculated on the portal. Timeline of about 15 working days is reported, not from an official AU page.

form_fields: WES / IQAS reference number (if for credential evaluation)
documents_to_upload: Authorisation letter (if someone else collects it)
application.after_submission: Apply on the AU online services portal, pay the fee online, and keep the acknowledgement/reference number. The university verifies the records and issues the transcripts (about 15 working days reported), in a sealed envelope, sent to the address given or directly to WES/IQAS.
application.notes: Document list confirmed by three transcript services. The exact AU fee is calculated on the portal and was not retrieved; the 15-working-day timeline is reported, not official.

question: How do I get a provisional certificate from Andhra University?
answer: UNVERIFIED — based on a student forum answer, not an official AU page. Andhra University offers an online certificate service at aucoe.info: go to the site, click 'apply for certificates', fill in your registration number and mobile number, fill the application form, select the purpose (provisional certificate, or duplicate provisional certificate), upload any evidence asked for, and pay the fee online. A tatkal (urgent) option for a duplicate provisional certificate is reported to exist. Note: once the convocation is over and the original degree is issued, the provisional certificate stops being valid — apply for the original degree instead. question: How do I apply for my original degree (convocation certificate) from Andhra University?
answer: UNVERIFIED — AU-specific fee and process not confirmed from an official source. In general: after you finish your course, the original degree is issued at convocation. If you did not collect it then, or you need a duplicate because it was lost or damaged, apply through your college or directly at the university Registrar/Examination branch: get the application form for the original degree, fill it, attach the documents below, and pay the fee by demand draft or payment receipt. For a duplicate degree, an affidavit is also required. The certificate is usually sent by registered post to your address, or you can collect it in person from the Registrar's office.

question: I lost my marks memo / marksheet. How do I get a duplicate?
answer: Apply to the Controller of Examinations of your university in the prescribed format. Steps: 1) File an FIR at the local police station about the loss (for a lost or stolen marksheet). 2) Make a notarised affidavit on stamp paper stating how the original was lost or destroyed. 3) Fill the duplicate marksheet application form and attach the documents below. 4) Pay the fee — it varies by university (for example, Rs. 100 per marksheet at NIT Raipur, Rs. 750 for a marksheet and Rs. 1,500 for a degree at Sankalchand Patel University). 5) The university issues the duplicate, usually within 30 to 90 days, marked 'DUPLICATE' on top. If the original is only damaged (not lost), you usually surrender the damaged copy with the application and fee — an FIR is not needed, but an affidavit is generally still asked for.
documents_required: Duplicate marksheet application form (filled and signed)
FIR copy from the police station (for lost/stolen)
Notarised affidavit on stamp paper declaring the loss
Photocopy of the lost marksheet/degree (if available)
Government-issued ID proof
Passport-size photographs
Newspaper publication notice (required by some universities)
Fee payment receipt / demand draft
notes: SPU and NIT Raipur are official university sources and agree on FIR + affidavit + photocopy + fee.

form_fields: Course and year/semester of the lost marksheet
documents_to_upload: FIR copy from the police station (for lost/stolen)
Notarised affidavit on stamp paper declaring the loss
Photocopy of the lost marksheet/degree (if available)
Newspaper publication notice (if the university asks)
application.after_submission: The Controller of Examinations verifies the application and issues the duplicate marksheet, usually within 30 to 90 days, marked 'DUPLICATE' on top. If the original was only damaged, surrender the damaged copy instead of an FIR.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by official procedures of Sankalchand Patel University and NIT Raipur.

question: How do I get a character / conduct certificate?
answer: A character (conduct) certificate states that you behaved well during your course — it is asked for at admissions, jobs, and some scholarship applications. At many colleges it is applied for on the same common certificate form as the bonafide and transfer certificates. Steps: 1) Get the certificate application form from the admin office. 2) Tick 'Character certificate' and fill in your details and the purpose. 3) Attach the documents below and get the HOD's signature if asked. 4) Submit it at the admin office and collect it after the stated time (usually a few working days).
documents_required: Certificate application form (character certificate option ticked)
Fee payment receipt (for example, SBI Collect receipt)
Final or provisional degree certificate OR last exam marksheet
College ID card
notes: Based on the Government Engineering College, Vaishali certificate application form, which covers bonafide, transfer, character, and other special-purpose certificates on one form.

form_fields: Course, branch, and semester / pass-out year
documents_to_upload: Fee payment receipt (for example, SBI Collect receipt)
Final or provisional degree certificate OR last exam marksheet
application.after_submission: Submit the common certificate application form at the admin office (with HOD signature where required) and collect the character certificate after a few working days.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by the Government Engineering College, Vaishali certificate application form.

question: What is a course completion certificate and how do I get one?
answer: A course completion certificate is issued by the college to confirm that you have completed all the academic requirements of your course (classes, exams, and practicals), even if the university has not yet issued the degree. It is useful when you need to join a job or a higher course before the convocation. Steps: 1) Write a request letter addressed to the Principal stating the purpose. 2) Get it authenticated (signed) by your HOD. 3) Hand it over to the college office. The office prepares the certificate, gets the Principal's signature, and issues it — usually within a few working days.
documents_required: Written request letter to the Principal, authenticated by the HOD
Copy of college ID card
Last semester mark sheet (if asked)

form_fields: Purpose of the course completion certificate
application.after_submission: The request letter, authenticated by the HOD, goes to the college office. The office prepares the certificate, gets the Principal's signature, and issues it within a few working days.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by MSSW office guidelines.

question: How do I download my AP EAPCET (EAMCET) hall ticket?
answer: Go to the official AP EAPCET website, cets.apsche.ap.gov.in. Click 'Download Hall Ticket'. Enter your registration number or payment reference ID, your qualifying exam (Intermediate/10+2) hall ticket number, and your date of birth. Your hall ticket will appear — check your name, photo, exam centre, and timings carefully, then download and print it on A4 paper. Take at least two printouts. Without the hall ticket you will not be allowed into the exam hall. If any detail is wrong, contact the exam authorities immediately using the contact details on the portal.
documents_required: Registration number or payment reference ID
Qualifying exam (10+2) hall ticket number
Date of birth (as registered)

question: My semester hall ticket is not generated / not showing. What do I do?
answer: UNVERIFIED — no official Andhra University page for semester hall ticket download was found, so this is the standard procedure across Indian universities. First check the three usual reasons: 1) Exam fee not paid or payment not confirmed — check the payment status with your transaction ID. 2) Attendance below 75% in a subject, or condonation not applied/approved — check with your department. 3) Pending dues (library, hostel, or college fee). If all three are fine, go to your college exam cell with your fee payment receipt and college ID card. The exam cell coordinates with the university Controller of Examinations to release the hall ticket. Do this at least 2 to 3 days before the exam.
documents_required: Exam fee payment receipt / transaction ID
College ID card
Attendance details from the department (if asked)
notes: UNVERIFIED: the steps are standard practice across universities, but no AU-specific hall ticket page or notice was retrieved to confirm the exact portal or office.

question: How do I apply for revaluation at Andhra University? What is the fee?
answer: Revaluation means your answer script is checked and graded again by a different examiner. At Andhra University: apply within 15 days of the result being published. The fee is Rs. 750 per theory paper for PG and professional courses (the revaluation form states this). For School of Distance Education courses it is Rs. 500 per paper. There is NO revaluation for practical exams, internal marks, project work, or viva — only theory papers. The fee once paid is not refunded. Get the fee payment challan from the Computer Centre or pay through the university portal, attach the payment proof, and submit the revaluation application form. Results are announced on exams.andhrauniversity.edu.in.
documents_required: Revaluation application form (filled)
Fee payment challan / payment proof (Rs. 750 per theory paper; Rs. 500 per paper for distance education)
Hall ticket number and registration number
Specimen handwriting on a separate sheet (asked on the SDE form)
notes: Fee confirmed from AU's own revaluation forms: Rs. 750 per paper (PG/professional, old batch form) and Rs. 500 per paper (SDE). The 15-day window is reported by findmycollege.

form_fields: Paper(s) for which revaluation is sought (paper code and title)
documents_to_upload: Fee payment challan / payment proof (Rs. 750 per theory paper; Rs. 500 per paper for distance education)
Specimen handwriting on a separate sheet (SDE form)
application.after_submission: Apply within 15 days of the result. The university gets the script re-graded by a different examiner and publishes revaluation results on exams.andhrauniversity.edu.in. The fee is not refunded. No revaluation for practicals or internal marks.
application.notes: Fee confirmed from AU's own revaluation forms. The 15-day window is reported by findmycollege.

question: What is the difference between recounting, photocopy of answer script, and challenge valuation (JNTU)?
answer: These are three different post-result services. Recounting (Rs. 100) only checks that all answers were marked and the marks were added up correctly — the answers are NOT re-graded. Photocopy of answer script (Rs. 1,500) gives you a copy of your evaluated answer book so you can see how it was marked. Challenge valuation (Rs. 10,000) is a full re-evaluation of the script by a teacher, and you can apply for it even after a photocopy evaluation if you are still not satisfied — within 30 days of the result. There is no recounting for laboratory external exams. Apply through your college Principal along with the attested statement of marks; the Principal submits it online through the university portal (emsrms). Late applications are not accepted.
documents_required: Requisition/application to the Principal
Attested statement of marks
Fee payment receipt (Rs. 100 recounting / Rs. 1,500 photocopy / Rs. 10,000 challenge valuation)
Evaluated photocopy of the answer script (for challenge valuation)
notes: Fees and procedure from official JNTUA Examinations Branch notifications (MCA Nov 2025 and B.Tech Dec 2023). Fees are per the notification for that exam — check the current notification for your semester.

documents_to_upload: Fee payment receipt (Rs. 100 recounting / Rs. 1,500 photocopy / Rs. 10,000 challenge valuation)
Evaluated photocopy of the answer script (for challenge valuation)
application.after_submission: Submit to the Principal, who forwards it online through the university portal (emsrms). The university processes it per the notification deadlines; late applications are not accepted. Challenge valuation can be applied for within 30 days of the result, even after a photocopy evaluation.
application.notes: Flow and fees from official JNTUA Examinations Branch notifications. Fees are per the notification for that exam.

question: How do I apply for supplementary (backlog) exams at Andhra University?
answer: UNVERIFIED — fee figures come from a secondary results site, not an official AU notification. In general: register for supplementary exams on the AU exams portal (exams.andhrauniversity.edu.in) before the last date. The fee is reported as starting at Rs. 600 for one paper and increasing for additional subjects, with a heavy late fee of about Rs. 2,000 if you register late. You need your registration number and hall ticket number. Check the official exam notification for your semester for the exact fee and last date, and do not miss the deadline — late applications are not accepted.

Exam fee payment (reported: from Rs. 600 for one paper)

question: How do I check my Andhra University result and download my marks memo?
answer: Go to the AU results portal, results.andhrauniversity.edu.in. Enter your 12-digit university registration number and your hall ticket number, and complete the captcha if asked. Your scorecard/marks memo will appear — download and save it, and take a printout. Results stay on the portal for only 30 days from the release date, so download your marks memo within that time. If you find a mistake in your name, father's name, or marks, contact the Controller of Examinations immediately with a written application and a copy of your hall ticket. If you are not happy with the marks, you can apply for revaluation or recounting within the timeline the university announces (revaluation within 15 days of the result).
documents_required: 12-digit university registration number
Hall ticket number
notes: The 30-day hosting window and 15-day revaluation window are reported by findmycollege; the portal address and login fields are consistent across sources.

question: How do I apply for the AP post-matric scholarship / fee reimbursement (Jnanabhumi)?
answer: Apply on the AP government portal, Jnanabhumi (jnanabhumi.ap.gov.in). Steps: 1) Register/apply online with your Aadhaar, course, and college details. 2) Take your Jnanabhumi application ID and Aadhaar number to a MeeSeva centre for biometric authentication. 3) The college verifies your application, and the government releases the money. The scholarship has two parts: RTF (Reimbursement of Tuition Fee — full tuition, special, and exam fee) and MTF (Maintenance Fee — Rs. 10,000 for ITI, Rs. 15,000 for Polytechnic, Rs. 20,000 for Degree and above, per year, for hostel and mess charges). Eligibility: family income below Rs. 2.5 lakh per year for post-matric (below Rs. 2 lakh for pre-matric), and no family member should be an income tax payer. Note: from the 2026-27 academic year, the amount is credited directly to the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account, and the student then pays the college fees — check the current process on the portal, because scheme names and payment modes have changed.
documents_required: Aadhaar card of the student
Caste certificate (SC/ST/BC/EBC/Minority as applicable)
Income certificate issued after 1 January 2026 (for 2026-27)
Bonafide certificate from the current institution
Previous year mark sheet
Bank account details (Aadhaar-linked; mother's account for MTF in some schemes)
Passport-size photograph
Fee receipt from the college
notes: Document list and income limits are consistent across sources. The 2026-27 change (money goes directly to the student's Aadhaar-linked account instead of the college) is reported by aimindia — verify the current scheme name and payment mode on jnanabhumi.ap.gov.in, because the scheme was earlier called Jagananna Vidya Deevena.

form_fields: Course, college, and year of study
documents_to_upload: Bonafide certificate from the current institution
Bank account details (Aadhaar-linked; mother's account for MTF in some schemes)
application.after_submission: Apply on jnanabhumi.ap.gov.in, then complete biometric authentication at a MeeSeva centre with your application ID and Aadhaar number. The college verifies the application online and the government releases RTF (tuition fee) and MTF (maintenance) amounts. From 2026-27 the money is reported to go directly to the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account — verify the current payment mode on the portal.
application.notes: Document list confirmed by multiple sources. The 2026-27 payment-mode change is reported by aimindia; verify on jnanabhumi.ap.gov.in.

question: How do I apply for a scholarship on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP)?
answer: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal, scholarships.gov.in. Steps: 1) Complete One Time Registration (OTR) with your Aadhaar card and an active mobile number, and get your OTR number. 2) Log in, fill in your education, caste, and family income details. 3) Select the scheme (central post-matric schemes for SC, ST, OBC/EBC/DNT, and disability students run on NSP). 4) Upload the documents below. 5) Submit and get your application ID; your institute verifies it online. The annual family income limit is Rs. 2.5 lakh for all four central post-matric schemes. Your bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) — a merely KYC-linked account is not enough. Note: the central post-matric scholarship for minorities has not accepted fresh applications since 2022-23.
documents_required: Aadhaar card and NSP OTR number
Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EBC/DNT) issued by Tehsildar/SDM
Income certificate of the current financial year (issued by Tehsildar/SDM)
Bonafide / enrolment certificate from the current institution
Previous year mark sheet
Bank passbook first page or cancelled cheque (account in the student's name, Aadhaar-linked)
Fee receipt from the institution
Domicile certificate (if the scheme asks for it)
Passport-size photograph
notes: The minority post-matric scheme status (not running since 2022-23) is reported by buddy4study, citing a July 2026 Lok Sabha confirmation.

form_fields: Course, institute, and year of study
documents_to_upload: Income certificate of the current financial year
Bank passbook first page or cancelled cheque
application.after_submission: Register with One Time Registration (OTR) on scholarships.gov.in, fill the application, upload documents, and submit. The institute verifies the application online, then the state/central authority sanctions it and the amount is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by Buddy4Study, Karvado, and CitizenNest guides.

question: What documents are needed for an education loan?
answer: Banks (and the Vidya Lakshmi portal) ask for three sets of documents. Student: KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, passport, address proof, photos), 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates, any completed degree, admission/offer letter, and the fee structure or cost of study from the college. Co-applicant (usually a parent): KYC, income proof — salary slips and Form 16 if salaried, or Income Tax Returns for the last 2 years plus audited financials if self-employed — and bank statements for the last 6 months. Collateral (only for secured loans, usually above Rs. 7.5 lakh): property papers, including the encumbrance certificate. Collect originals plus two sets of self-attested photocopies before visiting the bank. SBI typically processes a complete application within 15 working days.
documents_required: Student KYC: Aadhaar, PAN, passport, address proof, passport-size photos
10th mark sheet and certificate, 12th mark sheet and certificate, degree mark sheets if any
Admission / offer letter from the institution
Fee structure / cost of study document from the institution
Co-applicant KYC and income proof (salary slips + Form 16, or ITRs for 2 years + 6 months bank statements)
Collateral documents (only for loans above Rs. 7.5 lakh)
Scholarship award letter (if you have one)
notes: The college's part in this is the admission letter and the fee structure/cost-of-study document — see faq-001 and faq-003 for how to get those from the college office.

form_fields: Total cost of study (from the fee structure)
Co-applicant (parent/guardian) name, income, and employment details
Collateral details (only for secured loans above Rs. 7.5 lakh)
documents_to_upload: Student KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, passport, address proof, photos)
Fee structure / cost of study document from the college
Co-applicant income proof (salary slips + Form 16, or ITRs for 2 years + 6 months bank statements)
Collateral documents (only for loans above Rs. 7.5 lakh)
application.after_submission: Submit the application with documents at the bank or on the Vidya Lakshmi portal. The bank verifies documents, sanctions the loan (SBI typically within 15 working days for a complete application), and disburses the fee directly to the college against the fee demand letter.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by WeMakeScholars, StudyCapital, and FundMyCampus checklists. The college's part is the admission letter and fee structure — see faq-001 and faq-003.

question: Why was my scholarship application rejected or delayed?
answer: The most common reasons: 1) Aadhaar-DBT mismatch — your bank account is KYC-linked but NOT seeded with NPCI for Direct Benefit Transfer. Check the Aadhaar mapping at your bank branch or on the UIDAI portal and get it seeded. 2) Expired income certificate — it must be from the current financial year. 3) Wrong or mismatched bank details, name spelling, or Aadhaar number. 4) Institute verification pending — your college has not verified the application on the portal yet; ask the college scholarship clerk. 5) Missing or unclear document uploads. Fix the issue, and if the portal allows, correct and resubmit before the deadline. Over 35% of scholarship applications face delays for Aadhaar-DBT mismatch or incomplete certificates, so check these first.

question: I lost my college ID card. How do I get a duplicate?
answer: Steps: 1) Report the loss in writing to the college office or the student helpdesk / Lost and Found Cell. 2) Write an application for a duplicate ID card and get it signed by your HOD. 3) Pay the duplicate card fee at the accounts office — the fee varies by college (for example, Rs. 100 at some colleges, Rs. 150 at others, and Rs. 500 for a lost card / Rs. 250 for a damaged card at others). 4) Submit the application with the fee receipt at the office. The duplicate card is usually issued within 1 to 2 weeks. Carry your college ID number and a government photo ID when you go. If your card is only damaged, some colleges replace it free or cheaper if you return the old card.
documents_required: Written application for a duplicate ID card, signed by the HOD
Fee payment receipt
Government-issued photo ID (Aadhaar / PAN / passport)
Passport-size photograph (if asked)
Old/damaged card (if it is a damage replacement)
notes: Process is consistent across the cited college sources; the fee varies widely by college, so the app should not state one fixed fee.

documents_to_upload: Written application for a duplicate ID card, signed by the HOD
application.after_submission: Report the loss at the student helpdesk / Lost and Found Cell, submit the HOD-signed application with the fee receipt, and collect the duplicate card in about 1 to 2 weeks. The fee varies by college (Rs. 100-500).
application.notes: Flow confirmed by Chandigarh University, JVBI, and Salbari College sources. Fee varies widely — do not hard-code one amount.

question: How does the college library card and book borrowing work?
answer: At most colleges your student ID card IS your library card — show it at the library to borrow books. Borrowing limits vary by college: for example, undergraduate students may borrow up to 3 books for 21 days and postgraduate students up to 4 books. Always return books on time to avoid fines. Important: all library dues must be cleared and all borrowed books returned before the college issues a no-dues certificate, transfer certificate, or allows you to graduate. If you lose a library book, you must replace it with an identical copy or pay its current market value.
documents_required: College ID card (acts as the library card at most colleges)
notes: Borrow limits quoted are examples from Chandigarh University; each college sets its own limits.

question: How do I apply for hostel accommodation?
answer: Steps: 1) After getting admission into the college, apply for the hostel on the separate hostel application form — contact the Chief Warden (or warden) of the institute for the form and formalities. 2) Hostel admission is often based on merit where seats are limited. 3) Selected students pay the hostel fee — usually the full fee for the academic year in advance. 4) Hostellers must follow hostel rules and wear the hostel identity card on campus. Hostel fees and facilities (mess, gym, study rooms, laundry, medical room) vary by college, so check the hostel notice board or the Chief Warden's office for the current fee and rules.
documents_required: Hostel application form (separate form from the college admission form)
College admission proof / allotment letter
Passport-size photographs
Hostel fee payment (full year in advance at many colleges)
ID proof (Aadhaar)
notes: General process from the cited colleges. Andhra University's own hostel admission form, fee, and deadlines were not retrieved — the app should link the AU hostel office/notice for exact details.

documents_to_upload: Hostel fee payment (full year in advance at many colleges)
application.after_submission: Apply to the Chief Warden / warden. Where seats are limited, allotment is merit-based. Selected students pay the hostel fee in advance and must follow hostel rules and carry the hostel identity card on campus.
application.notes: General flow from JVBI, Salbari, and Chandigarh University sources. Andhra University's own hostel form, fee, and deadlines were not retrieved.

question: What is a no-dues certificate and when do I need it?
answer: A no-dues certificate (no-dues clearance) is proof that you owe nothing to any part of the college — no pending fees, no unreturned library books, no lab or hostel dues, and no fines. You need it when you: apply for a transfer certificate, finish your final semester, apply for a migration certificate, or need an NOC for graduation. To get it, take the no-dues form from the office and get it signed/stamped by each department in turn — your academic department, the library, the accounts office, the lab, and the hostel (if you stayed there). Then submit the completed form at the college office.
documents_required: No-dues form from the college office
College ID card
Library books returned / library clearance
Fee receipts showing no pending dues

question: Can I apply for certificates online, or must I go to the college office?
answer: Both, depending on the certificate. Many colleges now take certificate requests through the student portal/ERP, and universities run online certificate services — for example, Andhra University's certificate service portal (aucoe.info) handles transcript, provisional, and duplicate certificate applications online with online fee payment. But several certificates still need an in-person visit: the TC (you must surrender your ID card), and anything needing department signatures or original verification. College offices generally issue certificates between 10 am and 4 pm on working days. Check your college's student portal first — if the certificate is listed there, apply online; otherwise go to the admin office with the form and documents.
notes: Office timing (10 am–4 pm) is from MSSW's guidelines; AU's aucoe.info portal is reported in a student forum answer — see faq-015.

question: What is the 75% attendance rule?
answer: UGC and AICTE require a minimum of 75% attendance in each course (theory and lab) in every semester. Attendance is calculated per course, and in some universities also in aggregate for the semester. If your attendance falls below 75% in a course, you are not permitted to appear for the semester-end examination in that course — you are marked as detained for shortage of attendance. Attendance between 65% and 75% can be condoned in genuine cases (see the condonation question). Below 65% it cannot be condoned at all.
notes: Some universities (for example, SV University) also require 40% attendance in each individual course plus 75% in aggregate. The exact rule depends on the university's academic regulations.

question: My attendance is between 65% and 75%. How do I apply for condonation of attendance shortage?
answer: Condonation is allowed only for shortage up to 10% — that is, attendance between 65% and 75% — and only on genuine grounds such as medical reasons, sports/games, or NSS activities. Steps: 1) Write a representation letter to the Principal (through your HOD) stating the total classes held, classes attended, the shortfall, and the reason. 2) Attach proof: for medical reasons, you must have been admitted as an in-patient — attach the doctor's prescription, medical bills signed by the doctor/hospital, diagnosis reports, and the discharge summary, submitted within one or two weeks of discharge. For sports/NSS, attach the invitation letter from the organising institute and the participation certificate. 3) Get your parent/guardian's counter-signature where the college asks for it. 4) Pay the condonation fee per course after approval by the College Academic Committee — the fee varies (for example, Rs. 2,000 per course at some colleges, Rs. 500 per subject at VTU). Start at least 2 to 3 weeks before the exams. Condonation is not a right — the committee can reject it if the reason is not genuine.
documents_required: Condonation application / representation letter to the Principal through the HOD
Medical proof (for illness): doctor's prescription, medical bills, diagnosis reports, discharge summary
Sports/NSS proof: invitation letter and participation certificate
Parent/guardian counter-signature (where asked)
Condonation fee payment receipt
notes: Rules from JNTUK R25 academic regulations (official). The condonation fee varies by university/college — do not hard-code one amount.

form_fields: Total classes held, classes attended, and shortfall
documents_to_upload: Condonation application / representation letter to the Principal through the HOD
Medical proof: doctor's prescription, medical bills, diagnosis reports, discharge summary (for illness)
Sports/NSS proof: invitation letter and participation certificate
application.after_submission: The College Academic Committee reviews the application and documents. If approved, the condonation fee is paid per course and the student is allowed to write the semester-end exams. Apply at least 2 to 3 weeks before the exams. Condonation is discretionary — it can be rejected if the reason is not genuine.
application.notes: Flow confirmed by JNTUK R25 academic regulations (official). Fee varies by university — do not hard-code one amount.

question: What happens if my attendance is below 65%?
answer: Shortage of attendance below 65% shall in no case be condoned — this is stated in the academic regulations of JNTU, SV University, and most other Indian universities. You will be detained for that semester, which means you cannot write the semester-end examinations for the affected courses. You will have to repeat or re-register for those courses as per your university's regulations, and you may lose a semester. If you are falling behind, talk to your HOD and mentor early — once attendance drops below 65%, there is no condonation or medical certificate that can fix it.

question: My name is spelled wrong in university records. How do I correct it?
answer: For a small spelling mistake in college/university records: apply to your college exam cell or the university Controller of Examinations with a written application, your 10th class certificate (which shows the correct spelling), your Aadhaar card, and an affidavit if the office asks for one. The office corrects it and issues a corrected provisional certificate or marks memo — for example, JNTUK asks students with a name mistake to compare their SSC certificate with the provisional certificate, get the provisional certificate corrected, and upload the corrected copy. For a full legal name change (not just a spelling fix): you must first change the name legally — notarised affidavit on stamp paper, newspaper advertisement in one English and one regional-language daily, and publication in the Government Gazette — then submit the Gazette copy to the university to update its records.
documents_required: Written application to the college exam cell / Controller of Examinations
10th class certificate (shows the correct name spelling)
Aadhaar card
Affidavit (if the office asks for it)
For a full legal name change: notarised affidavit + newspaper advertisements + Gazette notification copy
notes: The internal university correction steps vary by university; the Gazette process for a legal name change is consistent across sources.

documents_to_upload: Written application to the college exam cell / Controller of Examinations
For a full legal name change: notarised affidavit + newspaper advertisements + Gazette notification copy
application.after_submission: The exam cell verifies the documents against the SSC certificate and issues a corrected provisional certificate or marks memo. A full legal name change must first be done through affidavit + newspaper ads + Gazette publication, and the Gazette copy is then submitted to the university.
application.notes: Internal correction steps vary by university; the Gazette process for a legal name change is consistent across sources.

question: My date of birth is wrong in my records. How do I correct it?
answer: Date of birth correction is treated as a rectification of an error, and it needs stronger proof than a name correction, because age affects exam and job eligibility. Steps: 1) Collect proof of the correct date of birth — your birth certificate issued by the municipal authority is the main document, plus your school leaving certificate or marksheet. 2) Make a notarised affidavit stating the incorrect and correct dates of birth. 3) For a Gazette notification, publish the correction and submit the application with your ID proof. 4) Submit the affidavit, Gazette copy, and supporting documents to your college exam cell / university Controller of Examinations to update the records. Approval can take 30 to 60 days or more, and applications go through strict checking. In some cases a court order is also asked for.
documents_required: Birth certificate issued by the municipal authority
Affidavit for date of birth correction (notarised)
School leaving certificate or marksheet
ID proof showing the incorrect date of birth
Gazette notification copy (where required)
Court order (in some cases)

form_fields: Date of birth as in records
documents_to_upload: Birth certificate issued by the municipal authority
Notarised affidavit for date of birth correction
ID proof showing the incorrect date of birth
application.after_submission: Submit the affidavit and proof to the college exam cell / university Controller of Examinations. Applications go through strict checking and approval can take 30 to 60 days or more.

question: There is a mistake in my marks memo / hall ticket (name, father's name, or marks). What do I do?
answer: Act immediately — do not wait until the exams or counselling. For Andhra University: contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) with a formal written application and a copy of your hall ticket, stating exactly what is wrong and what the correct detail is. For JNTUK's online degree (OD) applications, the same kinds of mistakes are fixed by uploading corrected documents: a photo problem needs a clear scanned photo; a name or father's name mistake needs the corrected provisional certificate (compare your SSC certificate with the provisional certificate); a memos problem needs clear scanned copies of all memos. Keep copies of everything you submit, and follow up with the exam branch until the corrected memo is issued.
documents_required: Written application to the Controller of Examinations
Copy of hall ticket
10th class (SSC) certificate (for name / father's name mistakes)
Corrected provisional certificate (where asked)
Clear scanned copies of all memos (for memo problems)
Clear scanned photograph (for photo problems)
